correctness.rationale: For three zeros a square has either zero zeros or one zero in each half. Zero-zero types correspond exactly to all-one runs. For two-zero types, integer-start feasibility for consecutive selected zeros reduces to the explicit lower and upper half-length bounds; all nine endpoint comparisons were reconstructed. After ordering the three gaps, the middle interval lies inside the minimum-gap interval and the largest-gap interval reaches the maximum allowed half-length. Counting its complement against zero-free types yields the closed formula, including the sole missing baseline length when the largest gap is even. Parity forces the smallest-gap interval to compensate before or at this missing length, proving every prefix inequality. The extracted checker directly enumerates 14665 odd words through length 29, compares their type sets to the formula, verifies prefixes, and checks 250 seeded gap triples. Finite experiments corroborate but do not prove the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 source explicitly conjectures all odd-length prefix inequalities, proves only the two smallest prefix cases and treats the two-run circular class. Neither its distinct-factor lower bound nor the 1997 weaker bound logically entails a non-equivalent type inequality for this three-marker family. The 2026 sparse-letter theorem concerns linear factors. Exact three-gap intervals and the resulting new infinite family of prefix inequalities are not covered by inspected primary material or comparisons with the two-marker statement. Equivalence or overlooked arguments in unindexed literature remain a real priority risk.

value.rationale: The work establishes every prefix inequality in a fresh explicit open problem for an infinite and naturally parameterized three-minority-letter family, not just for short words. An exact O(1) cardinality formula and complete type spectrum from cyclic gaps explain how compensating extra small-length types prevent prefix deficits. This result is a structural tool for exploring higher minority-letter counts and has significance independently of a general unrestricted proof.
